decisions.reason: F2 incorrectly attributed estimator and loss-section measurability to def-measurable-space, but both are explicit Statement hypotheses. Restricted F2 to the specified sigma-algebra and included the loss sections in Given. Composed sections yield measurable tail events even at an infinite threshold; separation makes their union the whole probability space, so finite subadditivity gives the 1/2 bound. This is a nonfatal fact-attribution defect; the Statement and Proof are unchanged.

The finite-product supplier uses i<N to define its factors, but does not require every later coordinate variable to retain those labels. X_1,...,X_N and Y_1,...,Y_N name the first through Nth coordinates, equivalently X_i=pi_(i-1) composed with X. This relabeling is measurable and preserves iid laws and the mismatch sum. At N=1, X_1 names the sole coordinate, so no coordinate is missing. The measurable-diagonal assumption ensures each mismatch event is measurable. No mathematical defect or edit is warranted.

F3 omitted the existence theorem hypotheses and F4 omitted the dominating measure and absolute-continuity hypotheses. Corrected both fact formulations. This is nonfatal to the argument: step 1.2 uses finite probability measures P_i and finite nu=P_0+P_1, proves P_i<<nu, and has AC in Given. Finite-valued nonnegative densities are therefore licensed; their difference is integrable, its positive and negative integrals both equal event-supremum TV, and the normalized parts and interpolation give probability-law witnesses. The zero-distance, epsilon=0 and epsilon=1 cases avoid division. Statement and Proof are unchanged.

Replacement expected and tail risks omitted the measurable-diagonal condition required by their coupling supplier. A two-point sample space with the indiscrete sigma-algebra is an allowed experiment, but its diagonal is not in the product sigma-algebra; hence the replacement model was invoked outside its domain. Added the condition locally to replacement risks, preserving all Huber laws and risk formulas. Measurable rules and loss sections yield measurable nonnegative losses and tail events, including t=+infinity. Finite product laws exist, and the identity coupling ensures a nonempty replacement supremum on its corrected domain. This is a fatal well-definedness defect of the original replacement interface, repaired without restricting Huber risks.
